dm:
Rain falls on the slate rooftops of Mourhold like ink, soft and constant, and hisses where it touches the enchanted braziers outside the Shade's Refuge. Lightning flickers over the Black Spires. Somewhere beyond the rain, bells toll. In Mourhold a funeral and a warning sound the same.

You stand in the Veiled Vigil, the high sanctum beneath the Refuge, its walls lined with books bound in flesh and iron. Elara sits close at your side in midnight blue and silver. Rhylla stands behind you with her arms crossed, watching the door. Eira kneels beside the altar of Elyndra. Galen leans against the wall by the map table. Koryth and Calyth have just come in from scouting the upper spires, wet and silent.

A coded message from Veyra Nox arrived an hour ago: "Red breath moves in the lower wards. The Ashen Veil sleeps with open eyes. Corvan's men sharpen law like daggers. The next shard pulses beneath us."

The Circle looks to you.

player: Shae calls the Circle to the obsidian table and says: 'We must strengthen House Velaris and take control of trade. Once we have a stronger foothold, we move out from under the Bleak Wards' shadow. Thoughts?'
dm:
The Circle gathers at the obsidian table, rain dripping from cloaks onto the stone. The brazier dims to a pulse.

Elara speaks first, low and warm. "Trade is blood. Let it flow through our fingers." She is master of the Shade's Refuge, your distant cousin and your betrothed, and she unrolls a scroll listing the merchant houses still unaligned. "Lady Celeste will move if we promise her routes west. Bellum Avarelle wants vengeance for Corvan's embargoes."

Rhylla tosses a coin on the table, one side stamped with the old Velaris crest, the other blank. "Velaris means loyalty, spies and fear. We take their gold or their tongues."

Galen asks about the streets. Eira says the name must become a beacon and a warning. Koryth warns that leaving Mourhold will make the Circle a threat to the whole world.

They are all waiting for your answer.

player: Shae takes Galen and Eira aside and asks them quietly whether they have had any more memories of the old lives.
dm:
Galen answers first, voice like iron dragged through gravel. He has said little in the Vigil all night. "Not memories. My hands know things. Formation drills older than any army in Vaenyr." He pauses. Some in the Circle call him Ash, and he lets them. "Once, half asleep, I called you the Firebrand. I do not know why."

Eira has not turned from the altar of Elyndra. She is an exiled priestess and a warlock, and the shadows gather thickly around her kneeling form.

"I feel it, but I cannot name it," she says. "I have been collecting old tongues that the others cannot read." She traces a sigil in the air. "In trance I said a phrase. Vel'asha Miren Tal. The Cycle, Returned."

Galen looks at you. Eira does not need to. Both of them wait to see what you will do with that.

player: Shae asks Koryth and Calyth what they found while scouting the upper spires.
dm:
Koryth sets down a rain-soaked map marked with red ink. He is the youngest of the Circle, a paladin in dented armour, and the Shard of Aurenis glows faintly under his collar. "Bleak Ward strongholds outside the capital. Six that we could mark." He hesitates. "The Crimson Wardens still remember when I was declared Champion of Valthir at the Broken Bastion. They might help. I am not certain we should ask."

Calyth is practical. She is a ranger who keeps close to Koryth, with a past in the wilds and in shadows. She taps the map east of the Blackward Coast. "A war band lives here. They are disgraced and exiled, but they fought in the War of Unraveling and they are loyal to coin."

Koryth watches you the way he always does, still unsure whether you are a chosen leader or a charismatic tyrant.

player: Shae asks Elara what she makes of Lady Maera Liss.
dm:
Elara folds the scroll and thinks before she answers. "Maera Liss is a noblewoman and a strategist. She is cool-headed and calculating, and she has been useful on trade reform. She admires your vision. She is an ally, not a member of the Circle."

Rhylla snorts from behind you. "She keeps close to you."

"Closer than I like," Elara admits, and does not smile. "Rhylla and I agree on very little, but we agree that Maera is competition for your attention. We keep it professional with her."

Galen says nothing, which for Galen is agreement. Eira says Maera's insights into the courts are real, but that she has never knelt at an altar.

The rain thickens against the windows of the Vigil.

player: Shae lays her gloved hand on the Shard of Sartha and asks the goddess what she wants.
dm:
The shard answers with a pulse that you feel in your teeth. The brazier gutters. Every shadow in the Vigil leans toward you.

The voice of Sartha is calm and old. She is the Old Goddess of Shadows, Sacrifice and Survival, and she has chosen you as her champion. "The gods lie." It is the same warning she gave before. This time she adds: "Adapt, child. Doctrine is a cage for the dead."

Eira lifts her head at the altar. When the shard quiets, she speaks as if reciting from memory. "There is a myth of the Gods' Stone. They say the gods were once one being, and the Stone is where the divine shattered. The shards of it bind their bearers to the gods who made them. I have found fragments, nothing more."

Koryth's hand goes to his own shard.

player: Shae asks Elara whether the goddess Valencia is on their side.
dm:
Elara tilts her head. "Not officially. She is the Goddess of Ambition, Desire and Social Ascension, the Gilded Flame. Her symbol is a gilded flame or a golden serpent, and her creed is 'To rise is to live. To settle is to perish.'"

She touches the corner of the map. "Merchants and nobles worship her. Celeste follows her ideals, so does House Durn, and I admit I do too, in my way. Using her name is useful with them."

Eira speaks from the altar of Elyndra, goddess of secrets, whose order keeps the quiet vigils of the Silent Veil. "Sartha will work beside Valencia when ambition serves survival. She fears ambition that has no leash."

Elara shrugs. "Valencia is a lever, not a patron."

The flames of the braziers shiver in the draught.

player: Shae asks Rhylla what the Bleak Wards are doing now and who leads them.
dm:
Rhylla leans against the map table. "The Wards are hurt and angry, which makes them careful. Their leader is Archon Varyn Morthal. Mind magic, illusion, patience. He serves Lir, the god of order, and he wants every shard in Vaenyr suppressed."

She shifts a counter on the map to the eastern docks. "They claim arcane security jurisdiction there. Ritual inspections, they call them. Celeste loses three caravans a tenday."

Galen speaks from the wall. "They serve order. Lir, and the other two, Kaelorith and Tyranna."

"They believe it," Rhylla says. "That is what makes them dangerous." She looks at you. "The Wards are still the strongest arcane power in Mourhold. They are just not as sure of it as they were a month ago."

The bells outside toll again.

player: Shae asks who stands beside the Archon in the Wards.
dm:
Rhylla counts them on her scarred fingers. "Aric Ironshade is their enforcer and military commander. Brutal discipline. His men do not question orders. Seraphine Lockeward is the mage-hunter and the archivist, cold and unyielding. She can detect forbidden magic and suppress it. And Alandar Redhammer, who carries a sacred hammer as executioner-judge. He sees mercy as rebellion."

She lowers her voice. "There is a rumour from the lower wards. The Wards are working on rituals against shard bearers, and bringing in divine enforcers to carry them out. I have no proof. Veyra's message about the next shard pulsing under us might fit."

Koryth's face goes pale for a moment. Elara says the rumour could be aimed at the Circle's families or allies.

Nobody in the Vigil has more than a rumour.

player: Shae asks about the Covenant of Lir and Duke Corvan.
dm:
Elara answers with the brisk precision of someone who has read a hundred reports. "The Covenant of Lir is the church side of the same coin. They have declared you a false prophet. Duke Elias Corvan leads them and rallies the traditionalists. He believes in rigid hierarchy and divine order, and he has been squeezing merchants with embargoes, Bellum most of all."

Rhylla adds, "Lady Ivette Ravenhall stands beside him. They are planning a gathering to reaffirm the old noble alliances. If he ties himself to the Bleak Wards, the scale tips."

Eira says that a reckoning with Lir's church is not a matter of if.

"He is not stupid," Elara finishes. "He is certain. It is worse."

The flame in the brazier burns low, and thunder rolls somewhere over the Black Spires.

player: Shae asks Elara to bring her mother to the Vigil. She wants to discuss House Velaris with Lady Maelis.
dm:
Lady Maelis Velaris enters with the cold grace of someone who has never been hurried in her life. She is regal and ice-eyed, in charcoal and slate blue with threadbare crimson at the cuffs, the old colours of House Velaris. The crest on her brooch is a broken crown pierced by a downward dagger.

She bows, not deeply, but enough. "Shaedryn."

Elara sits very still. Rhylla's hand rests near her knife. Everyone in the room knows that Maelis cast you out, and that she allied herself to the Bleak Wards while she ruled the house. Now she stands in the Vigil of the Refuge on your invitation.

She studies the room, the altar, the Circle. "You have built something I did not think possible," she says. "I did not come to flatter. House Velaris is yours in everything but the law. What would you have of me?"

The seat of the house, the Veiled Manor, stands dark across the city.

player: Shae takes her mother's hand and says: 'You swore at the Veiled Manor. Tell the Circle what you said.'
dm:
Maelis looks down at your hand in hers. Something moves behind her eyes, pride and old grief. When she speaks, her voice is quiet and exact.

"At the Veiled Manor you stood at the shrine of Sartha. You called on her to take me into the shadows, to bind me as she binds you. You held out your hand and told me that the houses of Mourhold are tools for a greater purpose. Join you, and House Velaris would rise like no other in a thousand years. Fight you, and I would scatter like dust on the wind."

She takes a breath. "I said, 'Then let the shadows take me too. For House Velaris.' And you corrected me. 'For us.'"

Elara, who saw it, nods once. "You wept, Shae. You went to your knees and held her legs and said you forgave her. Maelis called you her daughter. I think she will never forgive me for hearing it."

Maelis lifts her chin. "The shattered marionette was a fine touch," she says, and almost smiles.

player: Shae asks Maelis about Therrin and Darius, and whether anyone of that kind is left.
dm:
Maelis's face tightens. "Therrin was my cousin, and he was ambitious in the wrong way. He ran spies and cultivated Darius, and when you came back, they both planned to break you."

Elara speaks flatly. "Darius is dead. You saved the family from him. Therrin was executed after the purges. There was a spy, Harlon, who served Therrin's schemes. You gave him mercy, and Soraya took him in."

"The family did not like the purges," Maelis says. "But those who understood what they saw changed their minds. Tayla and Jared did. Some others took longer."

She looks at the map. "Therrin's fall made it possible for you to be seen as a protector, rather than an exile. I did not manage that in twenty years."

Her tone is not flattering. It is accurate, and she knows it.

player: Shae asks Maelis who in the family still stands in her way.
dm:
Maelis does not hesitate. "Thamiel."

Elara supplies the rest. "Elder Thamiel Velaris, Warden of Secrets. He keeps the family's ancient library and advises Archon Morthal in the Wards. Most of the forbidden knowledge in the house is his. He is loyal to Maelis, but beginning to question her strength."

"He wears old black robes," Maelis says, "and carries tradition like a blade across his back. You met him at the gala."

Rhylla recalls it. "You embraced him in public and asked whether it was time for a homecoming. He answered, 'You've always had a way of redefining expectations, Shaedryn. I suppose I shouldn't be surprised.' Morthal noticed."

"He is no longer your open enemy," Maelis says. "He is guarded, and he is intrigued. That is more dangerous than hate."

player: Shae asks Maelis about Evander.
dm:
"Evander Velaris," Maelis says, with the first real warmth she has shown all evening. "He is your cousin of the same generation. He represents the house at the High Court. I trusted him for decades. He is cool and calculating and, as far as I know, he is not married and has no attachments. House business takes all his time."

Elara nods. "He was neutral during the worst of the fracturing. At the Veiled Manor, you told him that you were the rightful heir, that you saved the family from Darius and purged the traitors. He agreed to support you."

"He also warned you," Maelis adds. "Temper power with unity, or the family breaks along a different line. He is aligned with you but watches every move you make."

Outside the Vigil, a bell tolls twice.

player: Shae asks what Tayla and Jared are doing.
dm:
"Allies," Maelis says. She sounds faintly surprised to be saying it. "They have been closer to you than anyone in the house, apart from Elara."

Elara smiles for the first time in an hour. "Tayla is a quiet observer, a minor socialite who watches everything. She was cautious. After the purges, she openly approved. Jared is a charming negotiator. He speaks for you in the family council and holds a swing vote there."

Rhylla grunts. "They helped reshape your story after Therrin was executed. They told the family you saved it, not threatened it."

"They were at a strategy meeting after the purges," Elara says. "They helped shape where the Circle would go next. I trust them."

Maelis folds her hands. "They are the closest thing to a faction you have inside the house. Do not waste them."

player: Shae says she wants to finish cleaning house. Thamiel will be won over or removed, and Evander kept close.
dm:
The words settle on the room like frost.

Maelis does not argue. "Thamiel cannot be bullied. He can be bought with knowledge or he can be broken with fear. Tradition is the only thing he believes in."

Elara makes a note on her scroll. "A private meeting at the Refuge, on your terms, would let you show him what the house could become. A public ceremony would pressure him. A failure either way would give the Wards a Velaris voice."

Rhylla says, "Or I could make him disappear for the afternoon." Nobody laughs.

Galen says, "Evander is neutral unless his interests are threatened. Keep that in mind."

The task is plain. Win Thamiel or remove him, and keep Evander, Tayla and Jared on your side. The family council still meets, and the Velaris elders are waiting to see what you do.

player: Shae asks Rhylla to tell her what the Shadowcloaks are now and who runs them.
dm:
Rhylla straightens. "The Shadowcloaks used to be the Graycloaks, a criminal syndicate. You reshaped them into the Circle's eyes and knives. We run intelligence, we carry messages, we purge when we must. We follow a code: discipline, restraint, subtle manipulation. No senseless violence."

She taps a spot on the map near the Refuge. "The Shade's Vigil is their base. A fortified site beside the Refuge, with an archive and a ritual sanctum. They answer to me through Lirian."

Lirian steps in from the corridor at the sound of the name. She is pragmatic, efficient and quiet, in a grey travelling coat. "Overseer of the Shadowcloaks," she says, with a small bow. "We are watching the docks, the Guildhall, and three houses. I can add more with notice."

Rhylla nods at her. "She is good. She does what she says."

player: Shae asks Soraya how the Shadowcloaks came to be, and what happened to Master Whisper.
dm:
Soraya Windstride waits by the door in worn leather over soft armour. She salutes with a fist to her chest. She was a city guard once, then a rogue, and now she mentors the Shadowcloaks.

"Master Whisper ran the Graycloaks," she says. "He was paranoid. He feared his own people. When he feared you, he tried to have you killed. The plot failed. The Circle took him in a swift ambush and he is dead."

"I recruited Jarek," she adds, nodding at the broad-shouldered man behind her. "Former city guard. He is steady, tactical, and he watches Lady Elara like his own sister. He would not leave her side if you ordered it."

Jarek says only, "My lady."

Soraya looks at you. "Some of us want war and some want silence. We need to know which you choose."

player: Shae asks Elara what she knows about Lady Celeste.
dm:
Elara unrolls the scroll and runs a finger down a list. "Celeste. A trader, charismatic and ambitious, and a patron of the Refuge at the Obsidian tier. She laughs easily, drinks wine as if it were water, and does not like being told no. The Bleak Wards block three of her caravans a tenday at the eastern docks, claiming ritual inspections, and Corvan's embargoes squeeze her further."

She taps the page. "Shared goals with you: stability in Mourhold, redistribution of power, a long partnership. Your relationship with her grew over private dinners. She is captivated by you. I will not pretend it does not bother me."

Rhylla looks out of the window. Eira murmurs that Celeste follows Valencia, which makes her loyal as long as ambition is served.

Elara adds, "She will help, if you give her routes."

player: Shae asks Elara to remind her of Bellum, and recalls aloud the oath in the Binding Parlor: 'I, Lady Shaedryn Velaris, stand with Lady Bellum. Our paths entwined, our purposes aligned, so long as we stand together. Should those paths diverge, we walk free.'
dm:
Elara listens to the oath without moving. "Bellum answered with her own words," she says. "'I, Lady Bellum, stand with Lady Shaedryn Velaris. Our paths entwined, our purposes aligned, so long as this bond holds true.' The sigil above your hands pulsed and vanished."

She describes the night. Lady Bellum Avarelle is a wealthy and cautious widow of a merchant lord. She lives at Silverhaven and carries a fan of chalcedony. She had declined the first invitation to the Refuge. You went to her, and you both entered in disguise, you tall with long blonde hair in a red gown, and she cloaked and masked.

"In the Hall of Echoes, the panels showed you a crown of shadows and linked hands. They showed her a glass mask and thorned vines. After the oath you took her to the Obsidian Baths."

She is careful. "It was personal. It was not romantic. I would have known."

player: Shae asks Rhylla about Veyra Nox.
dm:
"Veyra Nox," Rhylla says. "A smuggler, thirty-four or so, maybe the most capable in Mourhold. Dry, playful when she wants to be, and never on anyone else's terms. She dresses in understated silks."

She finishes her drink. "She used to be one of the Pale, the underworld outfit that once served the Nameless Shadow before it turned rogue. She is not Syndicate. She left the Pale when it started coming apart and the Wards moved in on its routes."

Galen says, "The Pale are splintering."

"Half think the Wards will protect them," Rhylla says. "The other half want to burn the whole thing down. Veyra stays out of the fire."

Elara adds, "She came to the gala at the Refuge. You won her over. She is an Obsidian-tier patron now and an informal ally. She offered an artifact and a secret as tokens. You promised her help if the Pale or the Wards move against her."

player: Shae asks about the Sable Syndicate and Silas Crowley, and whether Veyra has anything to do with them.
dm:
Rhylla shakes her head. "No. Veyra is not Syndicate. That is a different outfit."

Elara unrolls another page. "The Sable Syndicate deals in forbidden goods, black-market trade and artifact smuggling. They have been pushing into Circle territory, the Shade's Quarters. Silas Crowley leads them."

Rhylla describes him. "Early fifties. Tall, over six feet, lean as old bone. Pale skin, black hair silvered at the temples, eyes like melted silver. He wears a dust-coloured leather coat with Syndicate sigils too small to notice unless you serve him. His voice is low and dry. Rooms go quiet when he speaks."

"Sometimes an asset," Elara says, "often a liability."

There is something else in the Vigil. Eira has heard a rumour that Veyra deals with a remnant of the Pale, one of the groups that served the Nameless Shadow. She does not know if it is true.

player: Shae asks about the Merchant Guildhall and Guildmaster Vehris.
dm:
"The Merchant Guildhall is on the central market square," Elara says. "Gold chandeliers, vaulted glasswork, marble floors. The Conclave meets there."

She taps a drawing of a grey-haired man in a high collar. "Guildmaster Tolan Vehris. He controls shipping permits and licences. He is a pragmatist, driven by profit and stability. He tolerated the Wards' oversight of trade because it bought him security. He used to be allied with your mother, back when House Velaris held to order and the old arcane powers."

Maelis answers in the same tone. "I used him, and he used me."

"He resents your rise," Elara says. "He tried to suppress the Circle through trade policy, rumours and pressure on guild appointees. He is cold to you. He will vote against you."

Rhylla says, "Any man will sweat at a knife."

player: Shae asks who else will be at the Conclave. She has heard the names Halran and Liraine Vos.
dm:
Elara answers. "Liraine Vos is a noblewoman and a high priestess of Valencia's ambition. She is cunning, and a rival. She may try to block us at the Conclave. We have not found a clean way to neutralise her."

Rhylla supplies the other. "Halran Vos is her cousin. Mid-fifties, lean, nervous, always in House Vos garnet and gold, with a signet ring he wears like borrowed power. An old-money traditionalist. He holds the swing vote on dock access. He launders money for the Bleak Wards."

Elara adds, "There is a rumour about his daughter Ilaen. She married into House Quor recently. A missing dowry, illicit enchantments in the wedding gifts. Nothing public."

Rhylla smiles slightly. "He would sooner sit a vote out than see his name in the street. We have not approached him."

player: Shae asks about Hareth Dorne and Silva Dray.
dm:
Elara checks her notes. "Lord Hareth Dorne holds the rotating seat on the Conclave council. A minor and neutral house. He almost always sides with whichever bloc is winning."

"Silva Dray," Rhylla says, "is head of the Arcane Bazaar. Early to mid forties, taller than average, with near-black hair in a coiled crown threaded with silver. Pale grey eyes, almost silver, and skin like porcelain. She wears layered dusk-violet robes with drifting runes. A choker of living script. She doesn't smile."

Elara says, "She has ties to the Wards. Her charisma is eighteen. People fear to displease her more than losing coin."

"Have you ever spoken with her?" Rhylla asks.

Elara shakes her head. "No. She has never been in any scene with us. She is a gap in our map."

The fire cracks and settles.

player: Shae asks what exactly is being voted on at the Conclave.
dm:
Elara reads from a sealed paper delivered that morning. "The Eastern Docks Access Act. Officially, the Reallocation of Docking Rights and Arcane Inspection Mandates in Mourhold's Eastern Trade Corridors. It would strip the Bleak Wards of the right to interfere with trade inspections and hand oversight to an independent merchant commission."

"That commission would be stacked with allies," Rhylla says. "Celeste, and maybe Bellum."

The vote has five seats. Vehris will vote against. Celeste and Bellum will vote for. Halran Vos is the swing. Hareth Dorne holds the rotating seat and will follow the majority.

"If Halran does not vote against us, we win," Elara says. "Celeste asked for something specific. She wants the eastern docks open so her caravans can pass. She will owe you a real favour for it. Bellum wants discretion and security."

The Conclave sits at highsun tomorrow.

player: Shae asks Rhylla what House Rathven is, and whether Mira Rathven is anyone to know.
dm:
Rhylla's mouth thins. "House Rathven is a hard house. Military, rigid, loyal to tradition. They are allied with the Bleak Wards and with Lir. Lord Garric Rathven is the head, a hardline traditionalist who opposes you. His sister Lady Selyne is a strategist who does not like you. His nephew Edric has doubts about where the house is going."

She taps a corner of the map. "Garric has a daughter, Mira. Late forties, with long silver-blonde hair streaked grey, braided back and clasped with obsidian. Cold blue eyes. She wears black and violet robes sewn with constellations. She is a scout and an information gatherer. Impulsive. She acts without her father's approval."

"You have never met her," Elara says.

"A possible weak link in her house," Rhylla finishes. "House Travan holds a grudge against the Rathvens, too. That might help."

player: Shae asks about House Durn.
dm:
"House Durn," Elara says, "is merchant nobility. They worship Valencia and Kaelorith, ambition and knowledge. They are cautious. They prefer to hedge until power shifts. Lord Corvin Durn is the head, with Lady Isolde beside him."

She taps a name in the margin. "Their daughter, Ranna Durn. Not Renna, as one report spells it. Mid-thirties, human, tall and whipcord thin, with black hair braided in a double crown held with silver clasps. Dark hazel eyes. Olive skin. She wears slate and gunmetal."

Rhylla says, "She is the real strategist. Her father wears the title and she does the work. She resists the Wards through contracts and law."

"Charisma sixteen," Elara adds. "Unmarried. Undeclared. We have been courting House Durn with economic incentives. They are watching to see which way Mourhold falls."

The Conclave will matter to them.

player: Shae asks if there are any other rumours they have not dealt with, any people to watch.
dm:
Rhylla lowers her voice. "A man called Gregor is trying to use the Circle for his own gain. We don't yet know what he wants. An informant of ours, Evard, is keeping an eye on him."

Eira turns from the altar. "The Order of the Silent Veil is holding the Eclipse Vigil. It is a rare ceremony in honour of Elyndra's eclipse, when truth and secrecy blur. High Seeress Lyra Fellwind leads it, with Brother Ithran. We could gain favour with Elyndra's followers. We could learn something. We could be exposed."

Galen watches the door.

"We have not decided about either," Elara says. "Neither is urgent. But I would not forget them."

The night is late. The Conclave is tomorrow.

player: Shae writes to Bellum and Celeste to say she looks forward to seeing them at the Conclave, and signs as Shaedryn Velaris of House Velaris and the Shade's Refuge, and as Shae to Celeste. No mention of Sartha.
dm:
You write both letters by candlelight in the Vigil. Elara reads over your shoulder and points out one line, which you strike and rewrite. Sartha's title does not belong in a letter that will pass through merchant hands.

The black wax is stamped with the House Velaris sigil entwined with the Circle's mark. Soraya takes them herself and sets out for Silverhaven and Celeste's town house.

She comes back before the candles burn low, shaking rain from her cloak. Bellum sent back a single line on cream paper: "I will attend with the gravity you expect." Celeste sent a scrawl across the bottom of your own letter. "Dull affair, unless you are there. Seat by the fire is yours."

Rhylla reads the notes over your shoulder and snorts. "They like you."

The Conclave begins at highsun tomorrow.

player: Shae asks Rhylla to have the Shadowcloaks watching at the Conclave, and to escort her herself.
dm:
Rhylla is at the map table near midnight. Her coat is umber leather, fitted, and her daggers are visible but not flaunted.

"The Shadowcloaks will be watching," she says. "I have scribes, guards and servants inside the Guildhall. Soraya will be in the rafters. Lirian walks with the outer guard under false colours." She straightens. "And yes. I'll escort you myself."

She lowers her voice. "You shouldn't walk into that hall without someone who knows where every knife will come from."

The Guildhall has been scoured for scrying wards and alchemical sabotage. Lady Bellum and Celeste are expected. Liraine Vos may attend for Valencia. Thamiel's attendance is uncertain.

Rhylla pauses at the door. "You'll be flanked in shadow. But you won't be alone."

Then she is gone into the dark corridor.

player: Shae tells Rhylla to wear her best, and says that she will wear hers. Then she goes to her chambers and changes into House Velaris colours, less glamorous and more dangerous.
dm:
Rhylla's mouth curves, not quite a smile. "You'd turn a guildhall into a theatre."

In your chambers the dusk-glass mirror is fogged with shadow, a gift of Sartha that never reflects lies. The attendants are dismissed.

The regalia lies laid out. It is deep charcoal, slate blue and threadbare crimson, the old colours of House Velaris. The coat is a long fitted duster with a high collar and the crest sewn small: a broken crown and a dagger pointing down. Under it is matte-black leather woven with whispersteel thread. There is one asymmetric pauldron with the rune of Sartha in obsidian ink, barely visible. The knife from Rhylla goes on your hip. Elara's ring-blade goes in your boot.

No gown. No jewels.

You look once into the glass. It shudders but holds.

player: Shae kneels at the altar in the Vigil for a moment and asks Sartha for steadiness before the Conclave.
dm:
The Vigil is empty at this hour. The altar of Elyndra stands in its alcove, and the shrine of Sartha is a stone slab under a hanging lamp.

You kneel on the cold floor. The shard is warm under the glove. For a moment nothing answers. Then the shadows in the corner of the room draw together and thin, and the voice is not a voice but a pressure.

Sartha does not offer comfort. She says, "Do not make a promise you cannot pay." That is all.

Eira is standing behind you in the doorway. She has been there for some time. "I felt it too," she says softly. "She is closer. Every month she is closer."

She does not say whether that is good.

Beyond the walls, the first grey light of the day is touching the rooftops.

player: Shae asks Eira whether she has seen anything about the Conclave in the shadows.
dm:
Eira takes a long moment to answer. Her eyes are turned inward, the way they are in prayer.

"A hall full of light," she says. "Gold. Too much gold. I saw you standing in it and you did not look like a guest. I saw Rhylla at your side in red, and a man in garnet and gold who could not hold his cup."

She frowns. "That might be nothing. Elyndra's sight is thin when I ask for a particular day."

Galen speaks from the wall. "Whatever it is, I will be near the doors."

"You will be near the carriage," Eira says. "The Circle must not appear to have come as an army."

Galen says nothing. He does not argue. Eira's hand rests briefly on yours before she goes.

player: Shae asks Galen to guard the carriage and the streets outside the Guildhall.
dm:
Galen gives a single short nod. He asks no questions. "The east door, the carriage, the alley behind the grain merchants. I will have two Shadowcloaks on the roof across the square."

He checks the straps of his shield without being asked. He is a Vyrkani enforcer, a quiet man, and he has stood between you and an assassin's bolt before.

"Ash," you hear Koryth say from the door. Galen has told him that he may use the name. "I can take the second watch."

"You will stay with Calyth," Galen says. "You are the youngest. You are the one they want to see."

Koryth bristles and then nods. Calyth, behind him, says nothing and smiles very slightly.

The carriage is being harnessed in the courtyard.

player: Shae sends for Lady Maelis and asks whether she will attend the Conclave.
dm:
Maelis arrives dressed for travel, in dark grey with a single crimson thread at her sleeve. She does not ask why she was summoned.

"I have no seat at the Guildhall any longer," she says. "And Vehris would take my presence as an insult or an invitation. I'm not sure which." She looks at you. "I will stay at the Veiled Manor. If Thamiel comes to me, I will let him speak. I will tell you what he says."

It is as close to loyalty as she has come in public.

Elara watches her with a steady gaze. "You keep your oath?"

"I swore to the shadows," Maelis says. "I do not take that lightly." She almost smiles. "Go. Make Vehris sweat."

She leaves without another word, her footsteps even and slow on the stone.

player: Shae asks Elara for a moment alone before leaving.
dm:
Elara closes the door of the Vigil behind her. She is your distant cousin and your betrothed, not your sister, and the difference is something she makes sure you remember. She wears midnight blue and silver, with a ring on her left hand that you gave her.

"You are going to be magnificent," she says. "You are going to be terrifying. I'm going to be here, running the Refuge, and waiting for you to tell me how it went."

She kisses your gloved knuckles. "Come back. I don't care if you win. Come back."

Outside, the courtyard is loud with horses. Jarek stands at the gate, stiff-backed and watchful, ready to follow Elara wherever she goes.

Elara straightens your collar, though it does not need it. "Rhylla is waiting."

player: Shae comes down into the courtyard and looks at Rhylla.
dm:
Rhylla stands by the polished carriage, half in shadow under the hanging ivy. She wears a deep garnet evening gown, tailored sharp across the shoulders and slit at the side for freedom of movement. The cloth shimmers like blood in ink. A dagger lies hidden in the folds of the silk. Her hair is braided high and wrapped in a silver cord, the only nod to the colours of House Velaris.

She expected you in velvet. In power dressed to dazzle.

When she sees the charcoal and slate and crimson, she goes still, and her breath catches. "Of course," she says, barely above a whisper. "You remembered who we are."

She offers her arm, not as a guard. "Let them dress for court. We dress for conquest."

player: Shae looks Rhylla over, appraising. She says: 'Amazing. Just what I hoped for.'
dm:
Rhylla's eyes flick up to yours, a moment only. The corner of her mouth lifts, not a smile. Something more dangerous.

"You always did know how to dress your blade before you draw it," she says, and settles her cloak.

Then, quieter: "And I thought I would be the one disarming them tonight."

The door of the carriage stands open. Soraya, in plain livery, has taken the driver's seat. A pair of Shadowcloaks in dull coats trot on either side. Jarek lifts a hand from the gate. Galen has gone ahead.

The rain has stopped. Mourhold's streets shine like black glass under the lamps, and the Black Spires pierce a sky the colour of old iron.

Rhylla steps up first, then holds out her hand.

player: Shae steps down from the carriage in front of the Guildhall with Rhylla on her arm.
dm:
The square goes quiet as you step down. Servants stop talking. A herald at the top of the steps lifts his head. The light from the doors spills gold across the wet stone, artificial and hungry.

Rhylla takes your arm, her silk gown rustling over steel. Her face is unreadable, her eyes sweeping rooftops and doorways. Somewhere above, in the shadow of the eaves, a Shadowcloak shifts. Soraya's hand rests on the reins. Lirian, under false colours, has already crossed the square to the outer guard.

Inside, the buzz of the Conclave rises: merchants, guildmasters, minor nobles, anxious perfume. Lady Celeste and Lady Bellum are expected. Evander Velaris is somewhere in the crowd. Tolan Vehris will be on the dais. Halran Vos will be near a column of scroll-binders, alone.

The doors are open. The Conclave begins at highsun.
